hypothesis: Empty selection from reversed y bounds is a JS-only area-constructor error.
supportedSetup: Positive in-map integer rectangle endpoints; direct constructor check in one coordinate frame. No recorder or natural level route claimed for the reversed-y input.
expectedC: l_selection_fillrect loops y=y1; y<=y2; ++y without sorting. Reversed y is empty. Reversed x still fills via selection_do_line in each row.
observedJS: Reversed y returns zero points; reversed x has the same nine-point bitmap as the forward 3x3 rectangle.
control: Forward 3x3 yields 9 points; same-x vertical yields 3; reversed-x equals forward bitmap.
negativeProof: The suspected normalization contract is absent in C. y1>y2 makes the C loop execute zero times and the fresh selection remains empty; JS has the equivalent early return. For x reversal, C line walks backward and JS chooses xstep=-1. This is an explanation of the exact branch, not a claim about coordinate conversion or all area overloads.
